messages.author: 768a488c75e6cbd9
messages.subject: two coord_trans() at once?
parts:
I am trying to plot some data from the formants of English vowels.
Traditionally, we measure the first two formants (F1 and F2) and plot
reverse F1 on the Y axis and reverse F2 on the X axis. I'd also like
to do both axes on a log-scale, but ggplot2/qplot does not seem to
allow me to use multiple coord_trans(x=, y=) calls.

I've tried adding them to each other:

qplot(F2, F1, data=dat) + coord_trans(x="log", y="log") +
coord_trans(x="reverse", y="reverse")

which has the effect that the second overwrites the first. I've also
tried using:

coord_trans(x=c("log", "reverse") ...

in which case one argument is ignored. I realize I could plot -F2, -
F1, or log(F2), log(F1), but I don't want to. That'd be more
confusing, not less. But I'd argue this is a very natural thing to
want to do because:

1. flipping both axes renders each point in an approximation of the
left-saggital articulation space (e.g., higher F1: vowel articulated
with a greater oral closure, resulting from the tongue mass being
higher in the mouth).
2. These aren't linear with respect to human perception; most
psychoacoustic scales project them into log-space, and doing this
spreads the data out in a nice way.
3. Yet, as a community of practice, the numbers on the axis are still
meaningful: you might say "oh, that ae is really high, look...F1 under
600 hertz..."

So I wanted to perform both transforms at once, so the axis still says
"600", but the scale between breaks is logarithmic, and I don't see
why I should have to plot uninterpretable values just to get the scale
right, or vis versa.

So,

1. Is there any way to do what I want to do?
2. If not, should there be?

Yours,
Kyle Gorman

messages.subject: Re: two coord_trans() at once?
parts:
Thanks for your suggestion. This doesn't do what I want in two ways though:

1. It makes the breaks evenly-spaced in both logspace and the coordinate system of the graph, when I want only evenly-spaced breaks in logspace.
2. It also rewrites the values as exponents of euler's number, which is annoying.

Even if I ignored the breaks thing (which isn't that important since it doesn't change how anything on the graph looks except the axis), there should be a natural way to make the axes have the input scale and formatting (as opposed to powers of e). But the formatter argument doesn't seem to have a way to specify "default format", that is, the same way the numbers were input, as far as I can tell from the documentation.

Yours,
Kyle

messages.subject: Re: two coord_trans() at once?
parts:
sorry for not pointing to data earlier...it's at:

http://www.ling.upenn.edu/courses/cogs501/pb.Table

It can be read in w/ read.table("pb.Table", sep="\t", header=TRUE) and so on.

I tried what Dennis implied and Hadley made explicit earlier too, but it doesn't work. scale_x_reverse() and scale_y_reverse() appear, as far as I can tell, to multiply the internal representation of the numbers by -1, because then the coord_trans(x = "log", y="log")

The basic plot is:

p <- qplot(F2, F1, colour=Vowel, shape=Sex, alpha=I(1/3), data=dat)

To get that standard left-saggital view, I need to flip both axes, and then log both axes, or the other way around. BUT:

p + scale_x_reverse() + scale_y_reverse() + coord_trans(x="log", y="log")

Error in if (length(from) == 1 || length(to) == 1 || from[1] == from[2] || :
missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In match.fun(get(".transform", .))(values) : NaNs produced
2: In min(x) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
3: In max(x) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf

I bet it's getting NaNs when it tries to compute logs of negative numbers. If I try it the other way around, I get the same error. Whereas if I do all scale_*_*, or all coord_trans(), one just reverses the other.

I've posted two graphs online (so you don't have to download if you're not interested):

http://ling.upenn.edu/~kgorman/linscale.pdf

This has nicely marked axes, but is, in my opinion, begging for a log-log plot. The second, however, is in the logscale, but the axes are labeled as powers of e, which isn't very intuitive. I'd like the breaks to be natural for the data (so things like 1500, 1600, etc.), and the scale to be log. You get this with coord_trans(x="log", x="log"), as shown in:

http://ling.upenn.edu/~kgorman/logbreaks.pdf

but you can't combine it with reverse scaling. I imagine I can make my own breaks and axes labels, but it doesn't seem to fit with the larger model (in which coord_trans(), for instance, affects scales but not breaks, etc.), so I'm suggesting this is a bug, with all due respect to Hadley.

What I'd like to do, then, is:

- have reverse x and y scales
- have log-scale x and y
- have the breaks taken from the input data
- have the numbers formatted like the input data

But it appears to be "pick two or three of four" so far.

Thanks for everyone's help,
Kyle

ps: anyone trying to graph the data: "iy" should be in the top left and "uw" in the top right.

messages.author: d994cff5897faec8
messages.subject: Re: two coord_trans() at once?
parts:
While solving an entirely different problem, it occurred to me that it
would also solve this one. What you need is to define your own scale
transformation, which is undocumented but easy:

TransRevLog=Trans$new("revlog", function(x) -log(x), function(x)
exp(-x), function(x) exp(-x))
p <- qplot(F2, F1, colour=Vowel, shape=Sex, alpha=I(1/3), data=dat)

p + scale_x_continuous(trans=TransRevLog) +
scale_y_continuous(trans=TransRevLog)

You will probably also want to set your own breaks; when I do this I
get messy numbers on the axes (but not 10^anything ;-)

The arguments to Trans$new are: a name that doesn't seem to be used
for anything; the forward transformation you want; the inverse of
that; and the inverse to use when printing axis labels.

zw

messages.subject: Re: two coord_trans() at once?
parts:
Zack's solution worked for me, so I thought I'd share what I did. After defining that function, I:

p <- qplot(F2, F1, colour=Vowel, shape=Type, alpha=I(1/2), main='Peterson & Barney (1952) vowels', data=dat)
p <- p + scale_x_continuous(trans=TransRevLog, breaks=c(500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000)) + scale_y_continuous(trans=TransRevLog, breaks=c(200, 400, 600, 800, 1000, 1200))

Other than having to write my own breaks (which was actually nice to do), it works exactly how I wanted.

Kyle
ps: see upthread for the link to data if you want to replicate this.
